lead: Living plants and cultures a person keeps or grows, from houseplants, aroids, orchids, succulents and garden plants to fruit trees, seeds and bulbs, bonsai, cut flowers and mushroom, ferment and brewing cultures, organised genus → species → registered cultivar or strain → form, with breeders and craft traditions in the registers.

depts.note: One department for the arum family, everyday houseplants and collector species alike; genus is the kind, species and named cultivars are archetypes.

b.w: Aroid trade names are often unresolved; collectors prize correct identity.
Variegated collector aroids are priced on it.

b.v: established plant > rooted cutting > node > tissue-culture plantlet
b.w: How collector aroids are offered and priced.

s.brief: Kind = genus. Archetypes = key species then registered or widely traded cultivars (pothos: Golden, Marble Queen, N'Joy, Neon, Global Green, Cebu Blue (E. pinnatum); Monstera deliciosa, M. adansonii, M. obliqua, Thai Constellation, Albo; Philodendron hederaceum Brasil/Micans, P. erubescens Pink Princess, P. gloriosum, P. billietiae, P. melanochrysum, P. Birkin, P. Pink Princess etc.). Merge the old per-species Philodendron kinds into one Philodendron kind; old hybrid kind becomes archetypes. Source species via Wikipedia/Wikidata/POWO; cultivar names via maker or ICRA (International Aroid Society) pages. Add Rhaphidophora (R. tetrasperma 'mini monstera'). Detail axes: variegation, leaf form, plant size (node, cutting, established).

k.brief: Species archetypes (hederaceum, erubescens, gloriosum, billietiae, melanochrysum, verrucosum) then hybrids/cultivars (Birkin, Pink Princess, Prince of Orange).
Genus Epipremnum; Cebu Blue is E. pinnatum.

s.brief: Kind = genus. Anthurium: velvet-leaf collector species (clarinervium, crystallinum, regale, warocqueanum 'queen', veitchii 'king', luxurians) plus flowering A. andraeanum hybrids (Anthura is a breeder). Alocasia: reginula 'Black Velvet', micholitziana 'Frydek', baginda 'Dragon Scale', cuprea, zebrina, × amazonica 'Polly'. Merge old per-species kinds into genus kinds; species become archetypes. Add ZZ plant, peace lily, caladium, elephant ears (Colocasia). Aglaonema: Asian red hybrids from Thai/Indonesian breeders. Sources: Wikipedia/Wikidata/POWO, breeder pages.

depts.note: Non-aroid indoor plants; genus is the kind, species and cultivars are archetypes.

b.w: The RHS Award of Garden Merit marks a strong performer in suitable conditions.
No gnats, mould, scale or yellowing at purchase.
Place and light are the first filter for houseplants.

s.brief: Kind = genus or familiar group. Archetypes = main species then key cultivars (Dracaena trifasciata Laurentii/Moonshine, D. fragrans, D. marginata; Ficus elastica Tineke/Ruby/Burgundy, F. lyrata, F. benjamina; Pilea peperomioides; Begonia rex and cane begonias; Calathea/Goeppertia orbifolia, Maranta leuconeura). Old Rubber plant broadens to houseplant figs. Add ferns, palms, spider plant, Tradescantia. Sources: Wikipedia/Wikidata, RHS plant pages (AGM).

k.brief: Keep one genus kind Dracaena; snake plants (ex-Sansevieria) as archetypes.
Ficus elastica, F. lyrata (fiddle-leaf), F. benjamina.
Boston fern, maidenhair, bird's nest, staghorn (Platycerium).

s.brief: New shelf. Archetypes = species and named cultivar groups; African violet and Streptocarpus have societies and registers (African Violet Society of America; Dibleys for Streptocarpus). Poinsettia breeders (Dümmen Orange/Ecke). Sources: Wikipedia, society/breeder pages.

k.brief: Guzmania, Vriesea, Aechmea, Neoregelia; air plants stay separate.

s.brief: Hoya: species (carnosa, kerrii, pubicalyx, linearis) and cultivars (Krimson Queen, Compacta). Tillandsia: key species (ionantha, xerographica, caput-medusae). Terrarium: Selaginella, Fittonia, live moss (cushion, sheet, star moss) and marimo balls (Aegagropila, an alga; tradition note Lake Akan, Japan). Sources: Wikipedia/Wikidata, specialist nurseries.

k.brief: Types: sheet, cushion, moss ball; marimo as an archetype.

depts.note: Genus is the kind; archetypes are species and RHS-registered grexes, clones by awarded name.

b.v: AOS/RHS award (FCC > AM > HCC) > registered grex > unnamed hybrid
b.w: Awards and the RHS International Orchid Register mark recognised quality.
Blooming-size plants with spikes and buds are the buying norm.
Firm green roots, no rot or pests.

s.brief: Organise by genus (alliance), then archetype = species or RHS-registered grex (e.g. Paphiopedilum Maudiae, Paph. Prince Edward of York, Cymbidium Sarah Jean, Phalaenopsis schilleriana), version = awarded clone ('Cielo Azul'). Use the RHS International Orchid Register / Wikipedia / Wikidata as sources. Add Dendrobium, Oncidium alliance, Vanda, Miltoniopsis, Zygopetalum, Phragmipedium, jewel orchid (Ludisia), Neofinetia (fūkiran). Traditions: Japanese koten engei (fūkiran, shunran), Chinese lan (Cymbidium goeringii/ensifolium). Grex names in the t/details: no flat SKU lists.

depts.note: Genus is the kind; species then named cultivars and hybrids; Japanese hybrid lines and field numbers as versions.

b.v: species with field number > named cultivar > unnamed
b.w: Collectors track provenance (field-collection numbers) and registered cultivars.
Grafted rarities are priced differently from own-root plants.
Compact, unetiolated growth with no rot or mealybug.

s.brief: Archetypes: Echeveria species (elegans, agavoides, lilacina) and classic hybrids (Perle von Nürnberg, Lola); Sempervivum cultivars (Colorockz series as a breeder line); Aeonium 'Zwartkop'; Haworthia (Haworthiopsis attenuata, H. truncata, H. cooperi; Japanese hybrids); Aloe vera, A. polyphylla; Gasteria; Agave americana, A. victoriae-reginae, A. titanota. Graptopetalum paraguayense. Sources Wikipedia/Wikidata, RHS AGM, specialist nurseries.

Archetypes: Crassula ovata (Gollum, Hobbit), C. perforata; Kalanchoe blossfeldiana, K. daigremontiana; Sedum morganianum, S. spurium; Lithops species (C-numbers from Cole as versions); Euphorbia obesa, E. trigona, E. milii. Add string-of-pearls (Curio rowleyanus), Conophytum, caudiciforms (Adenium obesum, Pachypodium, Dioscorea elephantipes) for collectors. Succulent cuttings live in Seeds.

Archetypes: species then cultivars (Astrophytum asterias 'Super Kabuto', A. myriostigma; Mammillaria elongata, M. hahniana; Echinopsis/Trichocereus hybrids; Gymnocalycium mihanovichii 'Hibotan' grafted moon cactus). Add Christmas cactus (Schlumbergera), golden barrel (Kroenleinia grusonii), Ariocarpus, columnar cacti (Cereus, Pilosocereus), orchid cactus (Epiphyllum). Japanese hybrid lines as versions. Sources Wikipedia/Wikidata, Cactus and Succulent Society pages.

depts.note: Genus is the kind; species, then registered cultivars (ICPS register) and clones.

b.w: The International Carnivorous Plant Society registers cultivar names.
Temperate genera need winter dormancy and pure water.

s.brief: Archetypes = species then ICPS-registered cultivars (Dionaea 'Akai Ryu', 'B52', 'Dentate'; Sarracenia 'Judith Hindle', flava 'Redneck'; Nepenthes × ventrata, 'Bill Bailey', N. rajah). Trim old SKU lists into versions. Add Cephalotus, Heliamphora, bladderworts (Utricularia), cobra lily (Darlingtonia). Sources: Wikipedia/Wikidata, ICPS cultivar register pages.

depts.note: Genus or group is the kind; registered cultivars are archetypes, breeders sit in the brand register.

b.w: The RHS Award of Garden Merit marks a strong performer in suitable conditions.
Matched to your site, not a ladder.
Rose trials (ADR in Germany) and RHS assess it.
A named cultivar must look as named; PBR-protected cultivars come from licensed growers.

s.brief: Split the old filter kind into rose classes (WFRS/RHS). Archetypes = landmark cultivars with breeder and year: Peace (Meilland), Iceberg (Kordes), Graham Thomas and Gertrude Jekyll (David Austin), Just Joey, Albertine, New Dawn, Madame Alfred Carrière, Rosa rugosa, Gallica 'Officinalis'. Brands: David Austin, Meilland, Kordes, Harkness, Tantau, Poulsen, Weeks. Note ADR rose award and RHS AGM. Sources: Wikipedia, HelpMeFind Roses, breeder pages.

k.brief: Old filter kind; its types become these separate classes.
Modern shrub incl. ground-cover and patio.
Gallica, damask, alba, centifolia, moss, China, Bourbon, tea, noisette.
Rosa rugosa, R. glauca, R. moyesii.

s.brief: Archetypes = species and RHS AGM / landmark cultivars: Hydrangea macrophylla, paniculata 'Limelight', arborescens 'Annabelle'; Lavandula angustifolia 'Hidcote', 'Munstead'; Camellia japonica cultivars (trim old 12-SKU list to landmark ones with sources); Acer palmatum 'Bloodgood', 'Osakazuki', 'Sango-kaku'; Prunus 'Kanzan', 'Tai Haku', 'Shirotae' (Japanese sakura tradition); Clematis 'Nelly Moser', C. montana, C. armandii; Rhododendron/azalea (Exbury, Kurume, Satsuki); Magnolia × soulangeana, M. stellata; lilac 'Sensation'; Wisteria floribunda and sinensis; honeysuckle. Breeders: Proven Winners, Raymond Evison (clematis).

Archetypes = species and registered cultivars from society registers: Hosta (American Hosta Society: 'Sum and Substance', 'Frances Williams', 'Blue Angel'), Paeonia (lactiflora 'Sarah Bernhardt', 'Bowl of Beauty'; tree peony; Itoh 'Bartzella'), bearded iris (American Iris Society Dykes Medal), daylily (AHS Stout Medal), Delphinium Elatum, hardy Geranium 'Rozanne', Salvia 'Caradonna', Heuchera, ornamental grasses (Miscanthus, Calamagrostis 'Karl Foerster', Pennisetum), bamboo (Phyllostachys nigra, Fargesia). Sources: Wikipedia, RHS, plant-society pages.

Archetypes = series and cultivars from breeders: Petunia Supertunia and Surfinia (trim old 13-SKU Supertunia list to the series as an archetype with a few versions), Pelargonium (zonal, regal, ivy-leaved; scented), Fuchsia (hardy 'Mrs Popple'), Impatiens (New Guinea, SunPatiens), sweet pea (Spencer, Grandiflora; National Sweet Pea Society), Nicotiana alata, N. sylvestris. Breeders: Proven Winners, Suntory, Ball, Thompson & Morgan.

Archetypes: Nymphaea hardy cultivars from Latour-Marliac ('Marliacea Chromatella', 'Attraction', 'James Brydon') and tropical ones; Nelumbo 'Mrs Perry D. Slocum', bowl lotus (Japanese/Chinese traditions); add marginal and oxygenating plants. Sources: Wikipedia, IWGS (International Waterlily & Water Gardening Society).
Restraint only: turf types as t (ryegrass, fescue, Bermuda, zoysia).

depts.note: Fruit, nut and crop plants; chosen by variety first, then rootstock and form.

b.w: Fruit is chosen by variety first; RHS AGM varieties perform reliably.

b.v: M27 dwarf … MM111 vigorous; cordon, espalier, bush, standard
b.w: Sets final size and how it is trained.
Decides whether a partner tree is needed.

s.brief: Archetypes = landmark cultivars with origin and year: apples (Cox's Orange Pippin, Bramley's Seedling, Granny Smith, Golden Delicious, Honeycrisp, Braeburn; trim old list), pears (Conference, Doyenné du Comice, Williams' Bon Chrétien, nashi), plums (Victoria, Czar, Santa Rosa), peaches (Peregrine, Elberta), cherries (Stella, Morello, Bing), apricots, figs (Brown Turkey, Chicago Hardy), olives, pomegranates, persimmons (Fuyu, Hachiya), bananas (Musa basjoo, Dwarf Cavendish). Add quince, mulberry. Sources: Wikipedia, National Fruit Collection (Brogdale) pages.

Dissolve 'Other citrus trees' into a speciality-citrus kind (calamondin, Buddha's hand, kumquat, yuzu, finger lime). Archetypes: Washington navel, Valencia, Moro blood orange; Meyer lemon, Eureka, Tahiti/Persian lime, Kaffir lime; Satsuma, clementine; almonds (Nonpareil, All-in-One), walnuts (Franquette, Broadview), pecans, hazelnuts (Kentish Cob), sweet chestnut. Sources: Wikipedia, UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection.

Archetypes = cultivars: strawberries (Cambridge Favourite, Elsanta, alpine), raspberries (Glen Ample, Autumn Bliss), blueberries (Bluecrop, Duke), blackberries (Loch Ness, thornless), grapes (table: Black Hamburg; wine), elderberry, plus currants (Ben Lomond), gooseberry (Invicta), kiwi (Hayward, Jenny). Sources: Wikipedia, RHS.

Young and perennial crop plants (seeds are in Seeds & bulbs). Archetypes: basil (Genovese, Thai), mint, rosemary, thyme, bay; grafted tomato and chilli plants (heritage varieties); rhubarb (Timperley Early, Victoria), asparagus (Connover's Colossal, Gijnlim). Cannabis plant stays kind-level (legal status varies); cultivar names only where sourced from a reference page, no seed-bank SKU lists.

k.brief: Types: photoperiod, autoflowering; seed or clone.

depts.note: Propagating material: seed by crop, bulbs by genus; heirloom and trial-winning varieties are archetypes, seed houses sit in the brand register.

b.w: Seeds are chosen by type first.

b.v: AAS / Fleuroselect / RHS AGM > no award
b.w: Trial awards mark proven varieties.

b.v: bulb circumference in cm; certified seed potatoes
b.w: Larger bulbs flower better; certified seed potatoes are disease-free.

s.brief: Seed kinds by crop group; archetypes = heirloom and landmark varieties (tomato: Brandywine, Cherokee Purple, Moneymaker, Sungold; squash: Butternut Waltham, Crown Prince; beans: Cherokee Trail of Tears; radish daikon Minowase; zinnia: State Fair, Benary's Giant). Brands: Baker Creek, Johnny's, Thompson & Morgan, Suttons, Kings Seeds, Real Seeds, Sakata, Takii, Burpee. Old daikon kind broadens to root & brassica seed; zinnia to annual flower seed. Unrooted cuttings (succulent offsets, aroid node cuttings) kept as one kind. Sources: Wikipedia, seed-house pages, AAS winners.

k.brief: Types: succulent offset, aroid node, leaf cutting.

s.brief: Kind = genus; archetypes = RHS divisions/groups and landmark cultivars (tulip: Darwin hybrid, Triumph, parrot, 'Queen of Night', 'Black Hero'; Narcissus 'Tête-à-tête', 'February Gold', 'Thalia'; Galanthus 'S. Arnott' (galanthophile collecting); hyacinth 'Delft Blue'; Crocus tommasinianus; Lilium regale, 'Stargazer'; Allium 'Purple Sensation'; Hippeastrum; Dahlia 'Bishop of Llandaff', 'Café au Lait'). Seed potato (Charlotte, Maris Piper, Yukon Gold, Red Pontiac), seed garlic (hardneck/softneck), onion sets. KAVB/RHS registers as sources; Dutch bulb trade tradition.

depts.note: Kind = tree genus trained as bonsai; style and size class are types; bonsai, penjing and kokedama traditions in the register.

b.w: Root flare, trunk taper and movement are judged first in bonsai shows.
Price and care depend on stage.
Japanese pots (Tokoname) and display matter for show trees.

s.brief: Archetypes = classic bonsai species/cultivars: Juniperus chinensis 'Itoigawa', 'Kishu', J. procumbens 'Nana'; Pinus thunbergii, P. parviflora; Acer palmatum 'Deshojo', A. buergerianum; Ulmus parvifolia, Zelkova serrata; Satsuki azalea cultivars; Prunus mume, Chaenomeles, crabapple; Ficus microcarpa/retusa, Portulacaria, Carmona. Types on every kind: styles (chokkan, moyogi, shakan, kengai, han-kengai, bunjingi, yose-ue, ishitsuki) and size classes (mame, shohin, chuhin, dai). Traditions: Japanese bonsai, Chinese penjing, Vietnamese hòn non bộ, saikei, kokedama. Notable nurseries/masters (Shunka-en, Omiya Bonsai Village). Sources: Wikipedia, Wikidata.

depts.note: Fresh-cut plant material: florists' flowers by genus with named cultivars; Christmas trees by species.

b.w: Firm stems, buds just opening; growers and florists grade by stem length and head size.
Retailers and growers rank species by needle hold.

s.brief: Archetypes = leading florists' cultivars where a reference page exists (rose 'Freedom', 'Explorer', 'Avalanche'; chrysanthemum spray and disbud; Oriental lily 'Casa Blanca'; carnation; tulip; peony 'Sarah Bernhardt'). Keep bouquet and wreath as kinds with types. Tradition: ikebana (Ikenobō, Ohara, Sōgetsu schools) for arrangement. Sources: Wikipedia, grower/auction (Royal FloraHolland) pages.

k.brief: Trim maker list to a couple of sourced makers.

s.brief: Restraint only; types cut, pot-grown, rooted; sizes as detail.

depts.note: Spawn by mushroom species; ferment cultures by product; brewing yeasts by strain family with lab versions.

b.w: Live cultures lose vigour with age; labs date and count cells.
Brewers and growers pick by strain (e.g. Chico ale strain).
Clean spawn and cultures with no moulds.

s.brief: Spawn by species: kind = mushroom species; archetypes = named strains where sourced (blue oyster, pink oyster, king oyster; shiitake warm/cold weather strains; lion's mane; wine cap; Agaricus bisporus button/chestnut; reishi). Old carrier kinds (grain, sawdust, plug, liquid culture) and 'Other mushroom spawn' dissolve into t types on every spawn kind. Grow kit keeps types (log, block, bag, bed kit). Brands: North Spore, Field & Forest, Ann Miller's, GroCycle. Sources Wikipedia/Wikidata, supplier pages.

k.brief: Old carrier kinds dissolve into types: grain, sawdust, plug, liquid culture.
Agaricus bisporus; chestnut and portobello forms.

s.brief: Archetypes: San Francisco sourdough, heirloom starters (e.g. long-lived named starters where sourced); kombucha SCOBY and jun; water and milk kefir grains; koji spores (Aspergillus oryzae, tane-koji makers such as Higuchi Matsunosuke); yogurt starters (Bulgarian, Greek, heirloom mesophilic: viili, filmjölk, matsoni); vinegar mother. Brands: Cultures for Health. Traditions: Japanese koji, Caucasian kefir, Nordic viili.

Home-brew yeast strains: kind = yeast family, archetype = strain (Chico/American ale: WLP001, Wyeast 1056, SafAle US-05 as versions; London ale; Weihenstephan 34/70 lager; Belgian Saison; kveik Voss, Hornindal), versions by lab (White Labs, Wyeast, Fermentis, Lallemand, Imperial, Omega) and form (liquid, dry). Baker's dried yeast stays in Pantry Staples (J5). Wine yeasts: Lalvin EC-1118, Champagne, Bold Red; cider and mead. Algae: Spirulina, Chlorella cultures (trim to species archetypes). Sources: Wikipedia, lab strain pages.
